Monday. Nikhil was in charge of Friday's class quiz, and Miss Elizabeth had said he could choose how to do it. He wrote "questions", "score chart" and "prizes" on a page, and felt a knot in his stomach. Too much for one person. In the corridor he noticed Bhavna's notebook, with letters as tidy as print. "Will you make the score chart? I'll do the questions." "Yes," said Bhavna.

Wednesday. Nikhil had twenty questions ready. Bhavna showed him a chart with four team columns and empty boxes. "Is it big enough?" "Add a column for bonus points," said Nikhil.

Friday. The chart hung on the board, and Bhavna filled in the scores after each round while Nikhil read out the questions. Miss Elizabeth clapped.

qa.q: What did Nikhil ask Bhavna to make?
qa.a: Nikhil asked Bhavna to make the score chart.

qa.q: How was Nikhil feeling on Monday when he looked at the page?
qa.a: Nikhil felt overwhelmed, with a knot in his stomach, because it was too much for one person.

qa.q: What could Nikhil do to check that handing over the chart works well?
qa.a: Nikhil could look at the chart midweek, as he did, and agree what to do if Bhavna needs help.

qa.q: How might Bhavna have felt about being asked?
qa.a: Bhavna may have felt pleased and trusted, because her tidy writing had been noticed.

Nikita, you're trying to do the whole class party alone. Let your Sachin Chacha tell you about the class quiz I ran in Class 6.
Our teacher put me in charge. I tried to write the questions and draw the big score chart too. But my handwriting was like a chicken walking in ink. The chart looked terrible, and I'd only written ten questions by Wednesday. The quiz was Friday.
Then I thought of my friend Rukhsana, whose notebooks teachers showed to the class. I asked her, "Can you make the score chart? Five teams, ten rounds."
She made it that evening, neat and coloured. I spent Thursday only on questions and finished all forty.
On Friday everyone said the chart was beautiful. Nobody knew I'd asked for help, beti. And the quiz was better for it.

qa.q: How many questions had Sachin written by Wednesday?
qa.a: He had only written ten questions by Wednesday.

qa.q: How did Sachin feel looking at his own chart on Wednesday?
qa.a: He felt worried and embarrassed, since the chart looked terrible and the quiz was only two days away.

qa.q: When Sachin saw Rukhsana's neat notebooks, what choice did he make, and why did it help?
qa.a: He asked her to make the score chart, so he could spend Thursday only on questions and finish all forty.

qa.q: How might Rukhsana have felt making the chart?
qa.a: Rukhsana may have felt proud and trusted, since her neat handwriting was valued and everyone praised the chart.

grounding: It shows a boy running a class quiz asking a friend with neat handwriting to make the score chart while he prepares the questions.

The class quiz was on Friday, and on Wednesday Baljeet still had only fifteen of the forty questions. On top of that, Ma'am had asked for a big score chart for six teams, and his first try looked like a spider had walked across it.
He looked around the classroom at lunch. Bhavna was copying notes, and even her rough work looked like print.
"Bhavna, can you make the score chart? Six teams, eight rounds. I'll give you the team names."
She looked up, surprised. "Me?"
"Your writing is the neatest in class. I need to finish the questions."
She said yes. That evening Baljeet wrote twenty-five more questions and checked all the answers with his elder brother.
On Friday, the chart hung on the board, ruled and bright. Bhavna stood near it, pretending not to smile.

qa.q: How many questions did Baljeet have on Wednesday?
qa.a: He still had only fifteen of the forty questions.

qa.q: How was Baljeet feeling on Wednesday?
qa.a: He was worried and a bit embarrassed, with only fifteen questions done and a messy chart two days before the quiz.

qa.q: What else could Baljeet hand over next time, and why?
qa.a: He could ask someone to keep score during the quiz, so he can focus on reading questions clearly.

qa.q: How might Bhavna see being asked to help?
qa.a: Bhavna is surprised at first, then seems proud, standing near the chart and pretending not to smile.
